question: Does source revocation preserve current ownership and hash binding after an accepted chunk-ID reuse?
exploratory_information: Gate, datastore, traceback, revocation, documentation and original core tests inspected before freezing. Original offline suite: 32 passed, one optional pyarrow contrast skipped. No collision experiment scored yet.
design: All eight combinations of same/different chunk ID, principal and text in a two-ingestion sequence; real fresh Ed25519 signatures, no model calls or malicious payloads.
observables: removal of a current other-source record after revoking old principal
controls: New versioned IDs preserve replacement availability
repair_contract: Reject an existing chunk ID before mutation; admit changed versions with a new globally unique ID. This is an admission restriction, not transparent upsert or a concurrent transaction guarantee.
boundary: Local in-memory API behavior after controlled ID reuse; no claim of cryptographic break, production exploitability, poisoning-detection improvement, storage erasure or new general revocation algorithm. External caller authorization and global-ID allocation assumptions remain outside this experiment.
